| [0010](./0010/) | core | accepted | major | not-started | 2026-08-05 — D45 recorded and the plan closed against an audit of every decision in this entry and 0011. D45 SETTLES WHAT D43 LEFT OPEN: the version-major agreement is asserted in the identity package alone for #Module too, superseding D40's #Module half. D43 had declined to decide it deliberately, recommending symmetry on the record, and left it invisible to tooling — it is not an OQ, so `task questions:open` reported an empty queue while core-identity-shape carried both D40 and D43 and no answer. The exposure D43 accepts transposes unchanged and is restated rather than inherited silently: a module whose identity package is absent, hand-written or non-conformant carries no major-agreement check any consumer can run, because identity/identity.cue is never evaluated as a package by a consumer. It is bounded by 0011 D12's publish check and removed outright by D43's recommended follow-on, which is cheaper now that 0011 D21 and D22 both require core to ship the shapes. SEVEN PIECES OF DECIDED WORK HAD NO SLICE and now do. D36's LIBRARY HALF was the significant one — 06-operational.md assigned it to library while plan.yaml's library slices did not carry it, and it is real code: compile/match.go:111 reads schema.MetadataLabels (paths.go:71 == metadata.labels) to build the set match.go:350 tests requiredLabels against, with two further readers at compile/module.go:197 and schema/context.go:68. Shipping core's D36 without it would leave matching reading a field the design has emptied. It lands as a new `library-match-labels` slice together with two other orphaned match-path gates 04-graduation.md requires — D34's kube-aware transitive comparator (measured non-transitive today: v1alpha1 < v2, v2 < v10 and v10 < v1alpha1 all return true) and D10's own-dependency-graph test — and catalogs-identity-authoring now depends on it. D28'S TRAIT OPT-OUT had no home at all: the decision leaves only its SPELLING to the implementing slice, but the field itself is a core change that no integration point sited, so 02-design.md gains one and core-platform-and-match names it. D19's local-checkout render warning, D42's nineteen import sites across five repos (twelve in modules/, three in opm-operator/test/fixtures/ which the operator slice had described as taking no changes at all, two each in cli and library), and the testdata regeneration are added to the four slices that own those trees. D35's DOCUMENTATION DELIVERABLE gains a repo: 04-graduation.md makes it an implemented gate that the additive-only rule and the publish-only enforcement boundary are stated where a catalog author meets them, and until now `affects` carried no docs repo — opmodel.dev is added with a `docs-catalog-contract` slice. | [0013](./0013/) | cross-cutting | draft | - | not-started | 2026-07-27 — Design revised on review: D10 supersedes D1, D11 supersedes D4, D12 amends D9, and OQ1 is closed. D1 had removed the `#Secret` contract type AND the disjunction inside it, when only the routing metadata needed to move to the attribute — leaving the deployer no slot in which to say "this Secret already exists", and forcing the handle-plus-context-map machinery of D4 to compensate. D10 restores `#Secret` narrowed to `#SecretLiteral | #SecretRef`, so the ATTRIBUTE carries routing (author intent, static, in the published module) and the TYPE carries fulfilment (deployer choice, per environment, type-checked by CUE). D11 replaces handle substitution with resolve-in-place: the kernel rewrites every secret to its `#SecretRef` form, so both arms converge before render, a transformer reads two fields from one branch, and the whole handle format, the `#TransformerContext` addition, the `owned` flag and the output scanner are all deleted. Three properties fall out that the first draft lacked: instance files for supplied secrets do not change at all, plaintext in the render is structurally unrepresentable rather than stripped, and a secret interpolated into a rendered string fails at plain `cue vet` at authoring time. Experiment 02 rebuilt as `02-resolve-in-place` and re-run: all five claims held, and its Go content hash agrees with the CUE one in examples.cue. OQ2 opened — whether the arm rewrite survives the real kernel build path — and is now the sole blocker to acceptance. | Attribute-Declared Secret Fields |

## Status legend

- **draft** — initial design, actively being written
- **accepted** — design agreed upon, ready for implementation
- **implemented** — design has been realized in code
- **superseded** — replaced by a newer enhancement (see `superseded_by` in the entry's config.yaml)
